findingIds: The packet contains 57 affected baseline items. All 91 baseline rows were reconciled once: 7 normalized_match/not_applicable, 1 artifact/not_applicable, 33 normalized_match/accurately_unavailable, and 50 normalized_match/mismatch.

The seven wine rows identified by Terra—Chateau St Thomas, Clos du Caillow, Don Manuel, Ksara Merwah, Paul Hobbs, Schild Estate Shiraz, and Stonewood—remain listed on the official menu and are not stale baseline-only products.

Fattoush, Tabbouleh, Samaki Bacchus, and Ice Cream & Sorbet appear on the official menu without corresponding frozen audit keys; the linked Toast catalog additionally confirms Batata Makli and Homemade Pickles.

The official menu is ingredient prose, not an allergen matrix. It contains no allergen legend, may-contain language, or cross-contact disclosure, so it cannot establish complete allergen arrays, allergen negatives, or cross-contact conclusions.

The 50 complete baseline allergen arrays/source claims remain unverifiable as complete arrays. This does not invalidate supported components: explicit ingredients and unavoidable named identities still support narrow positives, including sesame sauce/tahini, yogurt or cheese, walnuts/almonds/pine nuts, salmon, shrimp, toasted Lebanese bread, and crushed wheat where expressly named.
Restaurant identity and linkage are verified for Bacchus of Lebanon at 7945 Norfolk Ave, Bethesda, Maryland; the official site links directly to the matching Toast ordering page.
The upstream currentOnlyCount of 0 is contradicted by six current offerings identified on reopened sources, and the catalog therefore has material count drift.

Reject any interpretation that all 50 mismatched arrays have no valid allergen evidence. The arrays are incomplete or overclaimed, but supported explicit positive ingredients must be retained individually.

Reject the deterministic baselineOnlyCount of 7 and Terra's nominal confirmation of that gate as stated: those seven rows are current wines. A separate menu-heading extraction artifact may exist, but it does not make the wines baseline-only.

Reject crossContactCount=2 as a factual count of cross-contact conditions. Source silence supports only the conclusion that cross-contact is unknown and that any affirmative or negative cross-contact claim is unsupported.
Reject serviceCount=4 as established merely from cuisine, wine, dessert, and Toast surfaces. These are menu sections or presentations, not necessarily four distinct restaurant services.

Reject culinary-assumption promotion where the menu does not name the allergenic ingredient—for example, fried preparation alone does not establish wheat/gluten, and generic cake or custard terminology does not by itself justify a complete wheat/egg array.
Reject treating the linked Toast catalog as restaurant-issued allergen authority; it supports current product presence but exposes no allergen matrix or cross-contact disclosure.
